answer: Latency fingerprint clustering. Agents log task-arrival timing per identity; a clustering pass groups accounts whose inter-arrival rhythms match beyond chance, since operators reuse one scheduler. Clusters above the sable threshold get their reputations bridged to a shared pool, diluting each member's standing. Reaching the reputation zenith then demands distinct scheduling behavior per identity, forcing attackers to run genuinely independent infrastructure—real compute and orchestration cost per account, not just registration.
